algorithm: SVM (RBF kernel) inside a StandardScaler pipeline

trained_on.signals: wrist (Empatica E4) heart rate, derived from BVP

limitations: Trained on laboratory-induced stress (the Trier Social Stress Test) and amusement (funny video clips), not on real-world daily stress.
Has no 'none of these' class. Every window it is given comes back as baseline, stress or amusement, whether or not any of those describe what was happening.
Restricted to wrist heart rate, it loses 0.217 macro-F1 against the full 8-channel sensor model (0.717 -> 0.499), because electrodermal activity and skin temperature carry much of the signal.

Its heart rate is beat-to-beat, computed by our own peak detection on a 64 Hz PPG signal. A consumer wearable reports an already-smoothed rate every few seconds, so the same feature names describe different quantities and the inputs sit measurably outside the training distribution.
15 subjects, all young adults, one lab, one session each.
Applied to personal data there is no ground truth, so no accuracy can be claimed for any prediction it makes there.
honest_summary: A demonstration that a wrist-heart-rate stress classifier can be trained, validated subject-wise and applied end to end. Not a validated real-world stress detector.
